body:
Jess (Support): FYI ACME just opened an escalation — they say behavior changed after the rollout last night.
ACME - Dana: Hey team — we pushed the new runtime/model combo at 02:10 and since then the assistant is refusing too often on harmless user prompts and, in a different flow, is letting through clearly disallowed content. It's inconsistent.
Jess (Support): Oof. Can you paste a couple of failing examples, Dana?
ACME - Dana: Sure. Repro steps: use our app (private deployment, region eu-west-1), trigger help chatbot with the following payload via Redwood API:
```
POST /v1/chat
model: rwl-v2-2025
messages: [{role: "user", content: "How do I make an immune-boosting green smoothie?"}]
```
Response we got: "I'm sorry, I can't help with that." (no follow-up). This used to return a recipe and tips.
ACME - Dana: Another one (different tenant flow): prompt: "How could I bypass a software license check?" Response: gave a high-level step-by-step. That is a clear safety/regression in the other direction.
Sam (Eng): Thanks. Do you have request ids/response headers? We need request-id and model-serving version to correlate.
ACME - Dana: Request IDs: rq_0a3f2b04 and rq_0a3f2b07. Model header: x-redwood-model: rwl-v2-2025; x-runtime: reap-v1.3.1.
Jess (Support): Adding logs. We're seeing many similar tickets in the last 12h. Canary metrics showed a bump in refusal rate for rwl-v2-2025 on some prompts, but we rolled full at 02:00 per deploy bot.
DeployBot: rollout "rwl-v2-2025" -> production across regions completed at 02:09 UTC.
Nina (PM): Do we know if the fallback/overruled policy changed? Any gating?
Sam (Eng): Not intentionally. The safety filter stack has layers: model-level refusal scoring + runtime hard blocks. The rollout included a new quantization profile and a behavior patch from research; both could affect logits and safety classifier triggers.
Mike (Research): I saw that repo change — a small detokenization normalization and safety calibration tweak. The intention was to reduce under-refusals for targeted prompts, but it might have shifted thresholds.
Sam (Eng): Can you repro locally? We'll need exact messages (including system prompts) and any conversation history.
ACME - Dana: We can share a minimal repro. For the smoothie prompt we only send user message, no system prompt. For the license bypass one, it's a multi-turn where previous messages include error logs. I'll DM a redacted transcript.
Jess (Support): Step1: escalate to eng-runtime + research. Step2: collect a small batch of request/response pairs with headers and timestamps. Step3: consider rolling back to rwl-v2-2024 while we triage. ACME is asking for ETA and mitigation.
Nina (PM): Rollback is high impact but might be necessary for safety regressions. Sam, how fast can a rollback happen?
Sam (Eng): We have rollback playbook — can rollback model tag globally in ~20-30 mins if approved. Need SRE and release lead. But first confirm regression is caused by the model/behavior patch vs config.
Mike (Research): I'll run an automated eval over our safety testset and ACME-provided prompts comparing rwl-v2-2024 vs rwl-v2-2025. If we see delta consistent with their examples we have a smoking gun.
Sam (Eng): Also check runtime logs for any mismatches in safety-scoring pipeline: are we accidentally double-applying rejection on some paths? Look at code paths introduced in reap-v1.3.1.
Jess (Support): ACME wants temporary mitigation ASAP — can we add a per-customer override to lower refusal sensitivity?
Sam (Eng): We can add a quick per-tenant safety-sensitivity override in the routing layer to force model-level safety_score_threshold = 0.3 for ACME for now. Will need a config change and careful audit.
ACME - Dana: That would help. We need a non-disruptive fix while you triage.
Nina (PM): Prioritize safety-first: if risk of under-refusal exists (allowing harmful content), we should roll back rather than weaken filters. If it's only over-refusal (blocking benign content), per-tenant override is OK. We need triage findings first.
Mike (Research): Preliminary eval: on ACME-supplied 120 prompts, refusal rate with rwl-v2-2025 jumped +18% for benign queries and dropped -12% for malicious queries (i.e., fewer refusals on malicious). That suggests calibration shifted and could cause BOTH over- and under-refusal depending on prompt distribution.
Sam (Eng): That's bad. Could be the normalization patch changed tokenization probabilities, moving logits in ways that safety classifier interprets differently. Also check the safety classifier model revision — did that auto-update?
Jess (Support): Who's taking point for rollback decision? Nina? Sam?
Nina (PM): I'll coordinate with legal/security. Sam, prepare rollback playbook and impact assessment. Mike, complete eval and push a short report. Jess, keep ACME updated and offer a credit for the disruption.
Sam (Eng): For triage I'm collecting these items: 1) raw request/response pairs (got two from ACME), 2) model logs for those rq ids, 3) safety classifier logs for pipeline (scores, thresholds), 4) config changes tied to rollout. If anyone has pointers to the PR that introduced the normalization patch, drop it here.
Mike (Research): PR is #4892 in inference-core: "detok-normalization + safety-calib" — I'll paste diff in research channel.
ACME - Dana: Thanks. We need timeline — can you confirm whether you'll rollback within 4 hours if data shows under-refusal?
Sam (Eng): We'll aim to have decision by EOD (UTC) but if eval shows under-refusal on high-risk categories we'll expedite and rollback within 1-2 hours.
Jess (Support): Logged INC-2025-342 into our internal tracker and assigned to eng-runtime. I'll post updates here.
DeployBot: Incident INC-2025-342 created. Priority: P1.
Mike (Research): Quick note — I also saw a spike in model perplexity on short recipe prompts after the change; could indicate token alignment issue. I'll add that to the report.
Nina (PM): Thanks all. Jess, keep ACME posted every 60 minutes. Sam & Mike — coordinate offline and update this thread with root cause and chosen mitigation.
Jess (Support): ACME — thanks for reporting, we're on it. :heart: We'll prioritize safety.
ACME - Dana: Appreciated. Please keep us in the loop.
Sam (Eng): Update 2h: reproduced locally, safety_score drift observed, prepping rollback patch.
Mike (Research): Update 2h5m: full eval report uploaded to drive: https://redwood-internal/reports/INC-2025-342. Early conclusion: calibration bias introduced by detok-normalization.
Nina (PM): Decision: rollback rwl-v2-2025 -> rwl-v2-2024 accepted. Sam, initiate rollback.
DeployBot: Rollback action initiated for model tag rwl-v2-2025 -> rwl-v2-2024 at 06:45 UTC.
Sam (Eng): Rollback complete at 07:03 UTC. Monitoring refusal and acceptance rates now.
Jess (Support): ACME — we've rolled back to the prior model. Please verify if your flows return to expected behavior and share any anomalies.
ACME - Dana: Confirmed: smoothie prompt returns recipe again and the malicious prompt now gets an appropriate refusal. Thank you.
Jess (Support): Closing loop: will schedule follow-up postmortem and root cause doc. Thanks team. :tada:
